content: Passions often engender their opposites: avarice sometimes produces prodigality, and prodigality avarice; one is often firm from weakness, and daring from timidity.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
